data.why: The GUI is a search form with no file upload; it queries the live public OpenAlex API at request time, so no local example data file is needed.

goals: Run a reproducible literature search for a review topic and retrieve a deduplicated results table
Compare source coverage (DOI, venue, abstract, citation counts) to decide which database(s) to rely on
Export the identified corpus to BibTeX or RIS for import into a reference manager
Export to Excel/CSV for manual screening or sharing with collaborators
Obtain a machine-readable search record and a ready-to-paste methods paragraph documenting the identification stage for a manuscript
Check whether any page of results failed to fetch, so an incomplete corpus isn't mistaken for a complete one

review.summary: The tree captures this tool's job well: running a reproducible search for the identification stage of a review, checking that every page came back, deduplicating with a record of where each value came from, and exporting in four formats. The phases and tasks are at the right depth, and most cited screens match their labels. It needs fixes before filing: the export tasks claim file contents that their screens don't show, and not_done includes two claims the code disproves (a search-record sheet in the .xlsx, and the shared file name treated as a bug). It also leaves out the default citation-count ordering and over-claims cross-source merging it never observed.
